expected_dimensional_complexity: moderate: BOP has many attributes, but selected series-key dimensions are COUNTRY, BOP_ACCOUNTING_ENTRY, INDICATOR, UNIT, FREQUENCY; scalar identity is compatible if only COUNTRY is removed and all other dimensions are retained.
expected_implementation_friction: moderate-high due to existing BOP task-local constants using campaign-specific source identities and because missing/whole-series distinctions must be made explicitly
expected_scalar_compatibility: compatible for selected aggregate current-account annual USD net-flow scalar series
expected_transport_behavior: metadata response large but stable; value acquisition likely requires country chunking to avoid long URLs/timeouts
release_identity_rule: derive acquired BOP as-of key from provider dataset UPDATE_DATE/PUBLICATION_DATE/Prepared evidence; do not use query-window bounds as release identity and do not invent official release semantics
selected_capability: Annual current-account balance and component net flows by country in USD, preserving IMF BOP accounting-entry, component, unit, scale, frequency, status, and as-of evidence.
selected_sectors_counterparts: Aggregate current-account components; no selected sector/counterpart split beyond component labels.
structural_assumptions_pressure_tested: source identity must be API/dataset not campaign
release/as-of identity must come from provider metadata
BOP component dimensions can be source-scoped scalar indicators
missing years inside returned series are explicit missing
whole-series absence remains distinct from missing observations
why_stronger_than_another_bis_or_small_p: The repository already has three recent BIS Phase 2 campaigns; IMF BOP closes a named external-sector gap (current account and components) and directly complements existing BOP financial-account, IIP, reserves, WDI external debt, and WDI trade evidence. This is higher marginal macroeconomic value than another BIS extension or small provider proof because current-account balances are first-order external-vulnerability inputs.
